rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī holds that a definite plural denotes the whole class; al-Ashʿarī, al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr, and Abū Hāshim dispute this, while emphasis and unrestricted exception support generality.
rows.anchor: أن لفظ الجمع المعرف بلام التعريف يفيد العموم ، والخلاف فيه مع الأشعري والقاضي أبي بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct address covers all people present at the time, but face-to-face speech does not directly address people who do not yet exist.
rows.anchor: يا أيهاالناس } خطاب مشافهة وخطاب المشافهة مع المعدوم لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later generations are included by separate, mass-transmitted evidence in Muhammad’s religion, which extends these commands to everyone until the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: عرفنا بالتواتر من دين محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أن تلك الخطابات ثابتة في حق من سيوجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken by genus semantics alone, the command to worship is discharged by performing one instance, since that instance brings the worship genus into existence.
rows.anchor: قوله اعبدوا معناه ادخلوا هذه الماهية في الوجود ، فإذا أتوا بفرد من أفراد الماهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī nevertheless takes every worship act to be commanded: worship as worship is the fitting cause of the command, since it expresses glorification and submission to God.
rows.anchor: ترتيب الحكم على الوصف مشعر بعلية الوصف ، لا سيما إذا كان الوصف مناسبا للحكم

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: An objector says unbelievers cannot be commanded to know God: if commanded while ignorant they cannot recognize the divine command, and if commanded after knowing Him the knowledge would already exist.
rows.anchor: لقائل أن يقول : قوله : { قدير ياأيها الناس اعبدوا } لا يتناول الكفار البتة لأن الكفار

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: The objector infers that unbelievers cannot be commanded to worship, because worship before knowing God is impossible and worship afterward depends on an impossible command to acquire knowledge.
rows.anchor: عبادة من لا يعرف ممتنعة أو يؤمر بالعبادة بعد المعرفة

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: The objection also excludes believers as addressees: they already worship God, so commanding them to worship would command an accomplished act.
rows.anchor: وأيضا يستحيل أن يكون هذا الخطاب مع المؤمنين ، لأنهم يعبدون الله

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: One reply says worship is conditional on prior knowledge, just as zakāt is conditional on owning the minimum threshold; these proponents regard knowledge as necessary.
rows.anchor: من الناس من قال : الأمر بالعبادة مشروط بحصول المعرفة ، كما أن الأمر بالزكاة مشروط

rows.speaker: من لم يقل بذلك
rows.claim: Those who reject that reply infer that knowledge is not self-evident: commanding worship also commands its prerequisite, knowledge, as purification, obtaining water, and seeking a deposit must precede their acts.
rows.anchor: وأما من لم يقل بذلك استدل بهذه الآية على أن المعارف ليست ضرورية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reasoning, an unbeliever can be addressed with worship, provided that he first believes and then performs worship.
rows.anchor: يصح أن يكون الكافر مخاطبا بالعبادة وشرط الإتيان بها الإتيان بالإيمان أولا

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: A remaining objection says commanding the acquisition of knowledge is impossible; Rāzī refers the full issue to works on legal theory and argues the objection need not apply to other attributes.
rows.anchor: بقي لهم : الأمر بتحصيل المعرفة محال ، قلنا هذه المسألة مستقصاة في الأصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To avoid treating believers as commanded to do what is already done, Rāzī reads the command as requiring continued or increased worship; added worship is still worship.
rows.anchor: لما تعذر ذلك فنحمله إما على الأمر بالاستمرار على العبادة أو على الأمر بالازدياد منها

rows.speaker: منكرو التكليف
rows.claim: Opponents of divine obligation argue that equal motives make choosing an act impossible, while unequal motives make one option inevitable and the other impossible; either way, the command exceeds capacity.
rows.anchor: قال منكرو التكليف : لا يجوز ورود الأمر من الله تعالى بالتكليف لوجوه : أحدها

rows.speaker: منكرو التكليف
rows.claim: They argue that divine foreknowledge makes the commanded act either inevitable, impossible, or unknown to God; the first two defeat the command and the last attributes ignorance to God.
rows.anchor: إن كان الأول كان واجب الوقوع ممتنع العدم فلا فائدة في ورود الأمر به

rows.speaker: منكرو التكليف
rows.claim: They deny a benefit in obligations: God cannot benefit from worship, while any benefit to people could be granted directly without hardship, making the hardship purposeless.
rows.anchor: فإن كان لفائدة فهي إما عائدة إلى المعبود أو إلى العابد أما إلى المعبود فمحال

rows.speaker: منكرو التكليف
rows.claim: They say people do not create their own actions; if God has already created an act in a person, ordering it is redundant, and if not, the order asks for the impossible.
rows.anchor: أن العبد غير موجد لأفعاله لأنه غير عالم بتفاصيلها ومن لا يعلم تفاصيل الشيء

rows.speaker: منكرو التكليف
rows.claim: They argue that obligations aim to purify the heart, so outward duties should lapse when they obstruct constant absorption in knowing God; jurists and analogists should follow rationalized rulings over appearances.
rows.anchor: المقصود من التكليف إنما هو تطهير القلب على ما دلت عليه ظواهر القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers the first three objections that their proponents must adopt the contradictory duty to believe that no duties exist.
rows.anchor: أوجبوا بما ذكروه اعتقاد عدم التكاليف فهذا تكليف ينفي التكليف وأنه متناقض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī’s theological reply is that everything God does is permissible, including imposing what people call an impossible burden, because God is creator and owner.
rows.anchor: عندنا يحسن من الله تعالى كل شيء سواء كان ذلك تكليف ما لا يطاق أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general command is qualified for those without understanding or capacity, including children, the insane, the unaware, the forgetful, and those unable to act.
rows.anchor: الأمر بالعبادة وإن كان عاما لكل الناس لكنه مخصوص في حق من لا يفهم كالصبي

rows.speaker: قائلون
rows.claim: Some also exempt slaves: the specific duty to obey their masters takes precedence over the general command to worship.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال إنه مخصوص في حق العبيد ، لأن الله تعالى أوجب عليهم طاعة مواليهم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī says the verse identifies God’s creation and beneficence as the reason worship exists.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : الآية تدل على أن سبب وجود العبادة ما بينه من خلقه لنا والإنعام علينا

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Rāzī’s school argues that servants do not earn reward from their acts: worship fulfills an obligation caused by God’s creation and favor, and fulfilling a duty earns no payment owed by God.
rows.anchor: أصحابنا يحتجون بهذه الآية على أن العبد لا يستحق بفعله الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding worship, the verse adduces the creation of the accountable people and their predecessors as evidence for the Creator’s existence.
rows.anchor: لما أمر بعبادة الرب أردفه بما يدل على وجود الصانع وهو خلق المكلفين وخلق من قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the verse establishes that God is known through rational inquiry and inference; he rejects the Ḥashwiyya claim that pursuing this science is an innovation.
rows.anchor: وطعن قوم من الحشوية في هذه الطريقة وقالوا الاشتغال بهذا العلم بدعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First reason for theology’s superiority: a science is nobler when its subject is nobler, and God’s essence and attributes are the noblest objects of knowledge.
rows.anchor: شرف العلم بشرف المعلوم فمهما كان المعلوم أشرف كان العلم الحاصل به أشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second reason: religious sciences outrank nonreligious ones, and exegesis, hadith, and jurisprudence all depend on theology’s establishment of the Creator, prophecy, and divine unity.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أن العلم إما أن يكون دينيا أو غير ديني ، ولا شك أن العلم الديني أشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third reason: theology is nobler because its opposites, unbelief and innovation, are among the vilest things.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أن شرف الشيء قد يظهر بواسطة خساسة ضده ، فكلما كان ضده أخس كان هو أشرف وضد علم الأصول هو الكفر والبدعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fourth reason: knowledge can be honored by its subject, need, or proof; astronomy illustrates noble subject, medicine greater need, and arithmetic stronger proofs, while theology combines all three.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : أن شرف الشيء قد يكون بشرف موضوعه وقد يكون لأجل شدة الحاجة إليه ، وقد يكون لقوة براهينه ، وعلم الأصول مشتمل على الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theology’s subject is exceptionally noble: it investigates God’s essence, attributes, acts, and the categories of what exists and does not exist.
rows.anchor: أما علم الأصول فالمطلوب منه معرفة ذات الله تعالى وصفاته وأفعاله ، ومعرفة أقسام المعلومات من المعدومات والموجودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its religious need is great because knowing these matters earns immense reward and association with angels, while ignorance brings punishment and association with devils.
rows.anchor: من عرف هذه الأشياء استوجب الثواب العظيم والتحق بالملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its worldly need is great because social order depends on belief in the Creator and resurrection; without that belief, disorder would spread.
rows.anchor: مصالح العالم إنما تنتظم عند الإيمان بالصانع والبعث والحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its proofs reach the highest strength because they are arranged with certainty from certain premises.
rows.anchor: براهين هذا العلم يجب أن تكون مركبة من مقدمات يقينية تركيبا يقينيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fifth reason theology is noblest: it is not subject to abrogation or change and does not vary among peoples or regions.
rows.anchor: وخامسها : أن هذا العلم لا يتطرق إليه النسخ ولا التغيير ، ولا يختلف باختلاف الأمم والنواحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sixth reason: verses on theological claims are nobler than legal verses; Rāzī contrasts the reported virtues of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, the end of al-Baqara, and the Throne Verse with verses on menstruation and debt.
rows.anchor: الآيات المشتملة على مطالب هذا العلم وبراهينها أشرف من الآيات المشتملة على المطالب الفقهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seventh reason: fewer than six hundred verses concern legal rulings; most others concern unity, prophecy, and rebuttal of idolaters, while stories teach God’s wisdom and power.
rows.anchor: وسابعها : أن الآيات الواردة في ا لأحكام الشرعية أقل من ستمائة آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī identifies five proofs of the Creator in these verses: creating accountable people, their predecessors, heaven, earth, and fruits from rain sent down from heaven.
rows.anchor: أولها : ما ذكر ههنا من الدلائل الخمسة وهي خلق المكلفين وخلق من قبلهم ، وخلق السماء وخلق الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s other signs in the heavens and earth likewise aim to establish the Creator’s existence.
rows.anchor: وكل ما ورد في القرآن من عجائب السماوات والأرض ، فالمقصود منه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge is shown by forming people in the wombs as He wills; effects and their ordering disclose the maker’s knowledge, just as theologians argue.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو عين دليل المتكلمين فإنهم يستدلون بأحكام الأفعال واتقانها على علم الصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse “Does He who created not know?” makes the same inference from creation to the Creator’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال : { ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير } ( االملك : 14 ) وهو عين تلك الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s keys to the unseen indicate knowledge of all things; fulfillment of reports about hidden events shows that He knew them beforehand.
rows.anchor: وقال : { وعنده مفاتح الغيب لا يعلمها إلا هو } ( الأنعام : 59 ) وذلك تنبيه على كونه تعالى عالما بكل المعلومات

words: وَفَأَخْرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزْقًۭا لَّكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different fruits and animals arising despite shared four-element natures show that God is powerful and freely choosing, not acting by intrinsic necessity.
rows.anchor: حدوث الثمار المختلفة والحيوانات المختلفة مع استواء الكل في الطبائع الأربع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī turns to Qur’anic proofs of divine transcendence, maintaining that God is neither a body nor located in space.
rows.anchor: وأما التنزيه فالذي يدل على أنه ليس بجسم ، ولا في مكان قوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As evidence for transcendence, Rāzī cites God’s proof given to Abraham against his people.
rows.anchor: وتلك حجتنا ءاتيناها إبراهيم على قومه } ( الأنعام : 82 ) وثانيها : حاله مع أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham challenged his father’s worship of an idol that could neither hear, see, nor help him.
rows.anchor: ياأبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغنى عنك شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham verbally challenged his people about the statues to which they were devoted.
rows.anchor: أما بالقول فقوله : { ما هاذه التماثيل التى أنتم لها عاكفون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham demonstrated the idols’ impotence by smashing them all except the largest, so that the people might turn to it.
rows.anchor: فجعلهم جذاذا إلا كبيرا لهم لعلهم إليه يرجعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the ruler, Abraham argued that his Lord gives life and death, exposing the ruler’s claim to do the same.
rows.anchor: { ربي الذى يحى ويميت قال أنا أحى وأميت } ( البقرة : 258 ) إلى آخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says sound minds recognize that kalām merely presents these prophetic proofs and answers objections to them.
rows.anchor: وكل من سلمت فطرته علم أن علم الكلام ليسي إلا تقرير هذه الدلائل ودفع الأسئلة والمعارضات عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham also asked God to show him how He revives the dead, addressing the afterlife.
rows.anchor: { رب أرنى كيف تحى الموتى } ( البقرة : 26 ) إلى آخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answered Pharaoh with the Lord who gave each thing its form and guidance, the same creation-and-guidance proof Abraham used of God creating and guiding him.
rows.anchor: قال ربنا الذى أعطى كل شىء خلقه ثم هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ appeal to the Lord of Pharaoh’s forefathers echoes Abraham’s argument that his Lord gives life and death.
rows.anchor: ربكم ورب ءابائكم الاولين } ( الشعراء : 26 ) وهذا هو الذي قاله إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Pharaoh demanded another proof, Moses named the Lord of the East and West.
rows.anchor: فلما لم يكتف فرعون بذلك وطالبه بشيء آخر قال موسى : { رب المشرق والمغرب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These proofs belong to the prophets’ practice: they reasoned them out and inherited them from their purified predecessors.
rows.anchor: التمسك بهذه الدلائل حرفة هؤلاء المعصومين وأنهم كما استفادوها من عقولهم فقد توارثوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses also argued for his prophethood by offering a clear miracle as evidence of his truthfulness.
rows.anchor: ففي قوله : { أو * لو * جئتك بشىء مبين } وهذا هو الاستدلال بالمعجزة على الصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad’s argument for monotheism, prophethood, and resurrection is unmistakable because the Qur’an is full of such proofs.
rows.anchor: اشتغاله بالدلائل على التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد أظهر من أن يحتاج فيه إلى التطويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an refutes materialists who say only time destroys by presenting various proofs.
rows.anchor: الدهرية الذين كانوا يقولون : { وما يهلكنا إلا الدهر } ( الجاثية : 24 ) والله تعالى أبطل قولهم بأنواع الدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Varied plants and animals arising despite shared natural temperaments and celestial influences refute those who deny a freely choosing Creator.
rows.anchor: حدوث أنواع النبات وأصناف الحيوانات مع اشتراك الكل في الطبائع وتأثيرات الأفلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s argument when night covered him refutes those who make celestial bodies partners by claiming they influence the world.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى أبطله بدليل الخليل في قوله : { فلما جن عليه اليل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an also refutes lower partners: Christians claim divinity for Christ and idolaters for their idols.
rows.anchor: وأما الشريك السفلي فالنصارى قالوا بإلاهية المسيح وعبدة الأوثان قالوا : بإلاهية الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One group denied prophethood altogether, asking whether God would send a human messenger.
rows.anchor: الذين طعنوا في أصل النبوة وهم الذين حكى الله عنهم أنهم قالوا : { أبعث الله بشرا رسولا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another group, including Jews and Christians, accepted prophethood in general but challenged Muhammad’s prophethood; the Qur’an answers their objections.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الذين سلموا أصل النبوة وطعنوا في نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وهم اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When critics objected to Qur’anic parables, God replied that He is not ashamed to give even a mosquito as an example.
rows.anchor: فأجاب الله بقوله : { إن الله لا * يستحى أن يضرب مثلا ما بعوضة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When critics demanded further miracles, including a spring from the earth, the Qur’an answered their challenge.
rows.anchor: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When critics objected to gradual revelation as grounds for suspicion, God explained that it strengthened the Prophet’s heart.
rows.anchor: كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an answers those who dispute resurrection with many proofs for the resurrection and against its deniers.
rows.anchor: الخامس : الذين نازعوا في الحشر والنشر ، والله تعالى أورد على صحة ذلك وعلى إبطال قول المنكرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To those who say obligations bring no benefit, God replies that good or evil deeds return to the doer.
rows.anchor: إن أحسنتم أحسنتم لأنفسكم وإن أسأتم فلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To the claim that determinism invalidates obligation, God replies that He is not questioned about what He does, while people are questioned.
rows.anchor: { لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون } ( الأنبياء : 23 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī abbreviates these examples because their full treatment appears elsewhere in the book.
rows.anchor: اكتفينا في هذا المقام بهذه الإشارات المختصرة لأن الاستقصاء فيها مذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since every prophet practiced this discipline, Rāzī concludes that its critic is either an unbeliever or ignorant.
rows.anchor: ثبت أن هذه الحرفة هي حرفة كل الأنبياء والرسل علمنا أن الطاعن فيها إما أن يكون كافرا أو جاهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rationally, taqlīd cannot justify choosing one authority: following everyone entails following unbelievers, choosing only some has no basis, and rejecting all imitation leaves rational inquiry.
rows.anchor: فهو أنه ليس تقليد البعض أولى من تقليد الباقي ، فأما أن يجوز تقليد الكل فيلزمنا تقليد الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture commands calling to God with wisdom and good admonition and debating in the best manner; Rāzī interprets wisdom as proof and demonstration.
rows.anchor: ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commanded debate concerns monotheism and prophethood, not legal branches: such branches are pointless to those rejecting prophecy, while those accepting it would not dispute the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لا فائدة في الخوض معه في تفاريع الشرع ، ومن أثبت نبوته فإنه لا يخالفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Muslims are commanded to follow Muhammad and take him as their example, they too must engage in the debate he was commanded to conduct.
rows.anchor: ثم إنا مأمورون باتباعه عليه السلام لقوله : { فاتبعوني يحببكم الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an condemns arguing about God without knowledge, which implies that argument grounded in knowledge is not blameworthy and is praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم } ( الحج : 3 ، 8 لقمان : 20 ) ذم من يجادل في الله بغير علم
